full_judgment:
2. Title Suit Nos. 134 of 1964 and 984 of 1962 were filed by the plaintiff respondents in the 1st  Court of Assistant Judge, Khulna for ejectment of the defendant-appellants as monthly tenants from Municipal holding Nos. 13 and 12 respectively. Admittedly the suit land measuring 0.17 acres being CS Plot No. 3871 appertaining to CS Khatian No.1865 of Mouza Baniakhamar originally belonged to one Rakhal Das Bose and his wife. The case of the plaintiff is that their predecessor in interest, Baidyanath Chatterjee purchased the suit land from the original owners in the benami of his relative Srish Chandra Bhattacharjee by a registered kabala dated 28-7-1927. Subsequently he divided the suit land into two equal parts and created two separate Municipal holding being holding No. 12 (new 23) and holding No. 13 (new 24). Baidyanath Chatterjee filed a suit being Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 in the Court of Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge), Khulna for a declaration that he purchased the suit land from the original owners in the benami of Srish Chandra Bhattacharjee who was his benamdar. On the basis of a solenama, a compromise decree was passed by the learned Subordinate Judge (now Joint District Judge) on 22-8-1958 declaring that Srish Chandra Bhattacharjee was benamdar of Baidyanath Chatterjee. Baidyanath subsequently transferred the suit property comprising holding Nos. 12 and 13 to the plaintiffs by a registered kabala dated 4-11-1961. The plaintiffs brought two suits, one 984 in 1962 another 134 in 1964 for ejectment of the defendants as monthly tenants from holding Nos. 13 and 12 respectively on the ground of default in payment of rent and bonafide requirement of the owner. 

 3. The defendants contested the suits by filing written statements denying the material allegations made in the plaint. Their case, in short, is that the defendants were never the monthly tenants of the plaintiffs or of Baidyanath; that no landlord and tenant relationship existed between them and Srish Chandra Battacharjee was not a benamdar of Baidyanath Srish Chandra Bhattacharjee died leaving two sons Dhirendra Bhattacharjee and Birendra Bhattacharjee, Baidyanath Chatterjee was the karmachary (employee) of Dhiren Bhattacharjee and Biren Bhattacharjee who migrated to India immediately after partition of India. Dhiren and Biren Bhattacharjee settled the suit properties along with other lands of the suit plot to defendants' predecessor in interest, Khondaker Abdus Salam on 17-5-1950 at a rental of Taka 30 on receipt of a salami of Taka 4001 by executing an amalnama (amaldari) and that the defendants have been possessing the suit holding since then on the basis of the aforesaid settlement. Their further case is that Dhiren and Biren Bhattacharjee agreed to complete the transaction by executing registered documents in favour of the defendants predecessor in interest but they did not do so. They also asserted that the solenama filed in Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 was fraudulent and the plaintiffs did not acqire any interest in the suit property by virtue of the kabala dated 4-11-1961. 

 7. Leave was granted to consider the submission that the High Court Division erred in affirming the decree for ejectment of the defendants from the suit premises as monthly tenants when there is no proof of landlord-tenant relationship between the parties and section 109 of the Transfer of Property is also not applicable in the facts of the case and the submission that the High Court Division upon a misconstruction of Exhibits 7, 8(a), 9 and 12(b) and the decree passed in Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 wrongly held that the defendants appellants were tenants under the plaintiff-respondents and their predecessor in interest, Baidyanath Chatterjee and the further submission that the High Court Division was clearly wrong in not adverting to the reasonings and findings given by the appellate Court in Title Appeal No. 295 of 1963 in which it was held that there was no relationship of landlord and the tenant between the plaintiffs and the defendants and accordingly, Title Suit No. 984 of 1962 was dismissed. 

 9. It is not disputed that the suit property originally belonged to Rakhal Das Bose and his wife. The plaintiffs' case is that Baidynath Chatterjee purchased the suit property in benami of his relative, Srish Chandra Bhattacharjee by kabala dated 28-7-1927 and Baidyanath Chatterjee possessed the said land and constructed huts. He let out the suit premises to the defendants who are monthly tenants. The further case of the plaintiffs is that Baidynath instituted Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 for a declaration that he purchased the suit property in the benami of his relative Srish Bhattacharjee who was his benamder. Dhiren and Biren, sons of Srish, filed solenama in the suit and a compromise decree was passed declaring Srish as benamder of Baidyanath. The further case is that by a registered kabala dated 4-11-1961 the plaintiffs purchased the suit properties at a consideration of Taka 8,000 from Baidyanath and late Khondaker Abdus Salam, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-4, was a monthly tenant in the premises at a monthly rent of Taka 15 under Baidyanath Chatterjee and thereafter under the plaintiffs and notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act was duly served upon the defendarit-appellants. 

 11. The learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the compromise decree obtained in Title Suit No.102 of 1958 by Baidyanath against Dhiren Bhattacharjee, and Biren Bhattacharjee, sons of Srish Bhattacharjee is not a transfer document and after the decree Dhiren and Biren did not execute any transfer deed in favour of Baidyanath and hence by such sole decree Baidyanath did not acquire any title to the suit property, We are unable to accept this argument of the learned Counsel as it is the definite case of Baidyanath that he purchased the suit land with his own money and for his benefit in the benamio"f his relation Srish Bhattacharjee and he himself was in possession initially by residing in the suit land and thereafter he left out the same to Khandaker Abdus Salam, predecessor in interest of the defendants as monthly tenant. Since the sons of alleged benamder Shrish Bhattacharjee filed solenama in Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 brought by Baidyanath for a declaration that Srish Bhattacharjee is benamder and the suit having been decreed on compromise on the basis of solenama filed by Dhiren and Biren, sons of Srish Bhattacharjee, in our view, no transfer document is necessary in favour of Baidyanath by Dhiren and Biren. 

 12. The learned Counsel then argued that since the defendants or their predecessor were/was not parties in Title Suit No. 102 of 1958 brought by Baidyanath against Dhiren and Biren, sons of Srish Bhattacharjee, they are not bound by the sole decree passed in Suit No. 102 of 1958. It is true that the defendants or their predecessor were not parties in the suit. In our view, they were not necessary parties in the suit and, as such, they were not rightly made parties in the suit. He next submits that Exhibits 7, 8(a), 9 and 12(b) were not properly considered by the High Court Division and upon misconstruction of those documents the High Court Division wrongly held that the defendants are tenants under the plaintiffs and their 'predecessor in interest Baidyanath. Exhibit 7 is the copy of the order dated 31-5-1950 passed by the House Rent Controller on a petition filed by the defendants predecessors, Khandaker Ansar Ahmed praying for fixation of rent of house No. 12. The House Rent Controller fixed the rent at Taka 15. Exhibit. 8(a) is the copy of an order dated 9-1-1963 passed by the Assistant Settlement Officer, Khulna in Objection Case No. 808 under section 19(1) filed by the defendant Khandakar Ansar Ahmed against the preparation of record of rights. It shows that record of rights was not prepared in the name of defendants' predecessor but order was passed to record his possession in Col. 13 of the Khatian Exhibit. 9 is the copy of reply to the show cause filed by the second party Abdus Salam in a proceeding under section 145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before Mr SA Hamid, Magistrate 1st Class, Khulna on 21-3-1958. In this petition he clearly stated that he came to the then East Pakistan in 1950 as a refugee and has been residing in holding Nos. 12 and 13 of Ward No.4 of Khulna Municipality (now City Corporation) as monthly tenant. Exhibit 12(b) is the copy of deposition of Khandakar Ansar Ahmed, in the above noted proceeding under section 145,Code of Criminal Procedure as second party. In his deposition he categorically stated "In 1950 we migrated to Pakistan and occupied the disputed house in holding No. 12 of Ward No. IV. We also occupied holding No. 13. Dhirendra Bhattacharjee is the owner of both the holdings. He lived in Calcutta. We are tenants of holding No. 12 and paid rent. Exhibit. A series are rent receipts granted by Bidhu Bhusan who was the karmachari of Dhiren, Exhibit. B is the certified copy of the suit register of the House Rent Control Case for the disputed house." In his evidence he also stated "We occupied the house after settling rent Taka 15 was fixed as rent for holding No. 12 from House Rent Controller in 1950. I have no paper to show the fixation of rent. Previous to the rent control case, we used to pay Taka 18 per month as house rent for holding No. 12 I have rent receipt for holding No. 13 which I will not file." In his evidence he further stated that he would deposit the rent of the suit premises before the House Rent Controller after disposal of the pending case. 

 16. This section provides that if the lessor transfers the property leased, the transferee acquires the right of the lessor and if the lessee so elects, the transferee shall be subject to all the liabilities of the lessor as to the property transferred. Since the plaintiffs acquired right, title and interest in the suit property through Baidyanath whose title was confirmed by sole decree passed in Title Suit No. 102 of 1958, it cannot be said that the defendants are not tenants under the plaintiffs in the face of Exhibits 7, 8(a), 9 & 12(b) and in view of our discussion made above. Hence the argument of Mr Ahmed does not stand.
